history.origins: Dates from the slave trade era, rooted in Yoruba culture of Nigeria, West Africa. Evolved into a card-based game during the colonial period and remains popular in Nigeria in the 21st century.
timeline: Slave Trade Era: Game emerges in Yoruba communities
Colonial Era: Standard 52-card decks adopted into the game
20th Century: Formalization of Professional vs Amateur rules
Present: Still played throughout Nigeria in families and youth centers
history.cultural: Important part of Yoruba social life; used for teaching arithmetic and inductive logic to children. High-stakes gambling game for adults. Known locally as 'scooping' game.
history.evolution: The game developed distinct rule variations: Normal Rules (allows duplicates in captures) and strict Yoruba Rules (forbids duplicates). Professional games use 3 rounds, amateur games use 4 rounds.

setup.players: 2 to 5 players. Professional games use 2 players; amateur games use 3-4.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Four special cards are removed: King, Queen, Jack, and 9 of Diamonds, placed face-up on the table as the initial palette.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 4 cards to start. Rounds continue until the deck is exhausted.

rules.objective: Capture the most cards from the table. Every card captured is worth 1 point at the end of the game.
rules.gameplay:
1. Players take turns playing one card from their hand.
2. Capturing (Scooping): A card can capture a table card of the same rank (Matching) or multiple table cards that sum to the played card's value (Summing).
3. Face Cards: K, Q, J have no numerical value and can ONLY capture their own rank.
keyRules: Jokers (if used in amateur games) can scoop the entire table.
Cards not scooped by anyone after the final round go to the player who made the last scoop.

strategy.basic: Memory is everything. Track which cards of matching ranks have already been captured so you don't save a card for a match that is impossible.
strategy.intermediate: Under Yoruba rules, avoid making 'obvious' sums. If you have a 10, don't leave a 7 and 3 on the table for your opponent; try to scoop them yourself first.
strategy.advanced: Esun Management: Build protected piles that require a high card (like a 10) to scoop, ensuring you have that 10 in hand before you start the pile. If an opponent sees your pile building, they may try to 'break' it by scooping components before you finish.
tips: Face cards (K, Q, J) are 'dead weight' if their matches are gone. Dump them early if the table is clear of their rank.
If playing with Isiwo, use it! Checking your pile helps you count the remaining ranks in the deck.

variations.name: Professional Rules
variations.description: Strict competition format: 3 rounds per game, no jokers used, applies Yoruba Rules strictly (no duplicate cards in captures), non-playing dealer as referee.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes round count and rules; no engine constant overrides needed.

variations.name: Amateur Rules
variations.description: Casual play format: 4 rounds per game, jokers (2 additional cards) may be used, Normal Rules apply (duplicates allowed in captures), more relaxed penalties.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes round count and allows jokers; no engine constant overrides needed.

variations.name: Esun (Building)
variations.description: Optional rule: Players can combine played card with table cards into protected piles that only they can later scoop. Pile must be scooped before next deal, otherwise player is penalized.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Optional rule adds building mechanic; no engine constant overrides documented.

variations.name: Isiwo (Card Viewing)
variations.description: Optional rule: Players may look through their own scooped cards at any time to track what cards remain in deck. Opponents' cards cannot be viewed.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Optional rule affects visibility only; no engine constant overrides needed.

scoring.description: Capture the most cards from the table. Every card captured is worth 1 point at the end of the game.
scoring.winCondition: Player with most captured cards after all rounds wins the game.
